source_text: Aller Anfang ist schwer
english_translation: All beginnings are difficult
Cultural_Context: Starting something new is always the hardest part — perseverance is key.

source_text: Der Apfel fällt nicht weit vom Stamm
english_translation: The apple does not fall far from the tree
Cultural_Context: Children often resemble their parents in character, behavior, or talents.

source_text: Besser spät als nie
english_translation: Better late than never
Cultural_Context: It's better to do something (even delayed) than never do it at all.

source_text: Der frühe Vogel fängt den Wurm
english_translation: The early bird catches the worm
Cultural_Context: Diligence and starting early bring success and advantages.

source_text: Was du heute kannst besorgen, das verschiebe nicht auf morgen
english_translation: Don't put off until tomorrow what you can do today
Cultural_Context: Act promptly — procrastination leads to problems.

source_text: Übung macht den Meister
english_translation: Practice makes perfect
Cultural_Context: Mastery comes from repeated effort and experience.

source_text: Kleinvieh macht auch Mist
english_translation: Small cattle also make manure
Cultural_Context: Small contributions or efforts add up to something significant over time.

source_text: Man soll den Tag nicht vor dem Abend loben
english_translation: Don't praise the day before the evening
Cultural_Context: Don't celebrate success too early — wait until the outcome is certain.

source_text: Wer den Pfennig nicht ehrt, ist des Talers nicht wert
english_translation: He who does not honor the penny is not worth the dollar
Cultural_Context: Value small things and be frugal — wastefulness leads to poverty.

source_text: Was Hänschen nicht lernt, lernt Hans nimmermehr
english_translation: What little Hans doesn't learn, big Hans will never learn
Cultural_Context: Habits and knowledge formed in childhood are hard to change later.

source_text: Der Weg zur Hölle ist mit guten Vorsätzen gepflastert
english_translation: The road to hell is paved with good intentions
Cultural_Context: Good intentions alone are not enough — action matters.

source_text: In der Kürze liegt die Würze
english_translation: Brevity is the soul of wit
Cultural_Context: Keep things short and to the point — conciseness is powerful.

source_text: Kein Rauch ohne Flamme
english_translation: No smoke without fire
Cultural_Context: Rumors or accusations usually have some basis in truth.

source_text: Wer A sagt, muss auch B sagen
english_translation: He who says A must also say B
Cultural_Context: If you start something, you must see it through or accept the consequences.

source_text: Der Mensch denkt, Gott lenkt
english_translation: Man proposes, God disposes
Cultural_Context: People can plan, but fate or higher powers determine the outcome.

source_text: Was lange währt, wird endlich gut
english_translation: What lasts long becomes good in the end
Cultural_Context: Good things take time — patience brings quality results.

source_text: Erst kommt das Fressen, dann die Moral
english_translation: First comes eating, then morality
Cultural_Context: Basic needs must be met before higher values or ethics can be considered.

source_text: Not macht erfinderisch
english_translation: Necessity is the mother of invention
Cultural_Context: Hardship or need sparks creativity and solutions.

source_text: Der Geist ist willig, aber das Fleisch ist schwach
english_translation: The spirit is willing but the flesh is weak
Cultural_Context: Good intentions are easy, but carrying them out is hard due to human weakness.

source_text: Steter Tropfen höhlt den Stein
english_translation: Constant dripping wears away the stone
Cultural_Context: Persistent small efforts eventually achieve big results.

source_text: Der Weg ist das Ziel
english_translation: The journey is the goal
Cultural_Context: The process and experience matter more than the destination.

source_text: Kleider machen Leute
english_translation: Clothes make the man
Cultural_Context: Appearance and presentation influence how people perceive you.

source_text: Was man nicht im Kopfe hat, muss man in den Beinen haben
english_translation: What you don't have in your head you must have in your legs
Cultural_Context: If you're forgetful or disorganized, you end up doing extra work.

source_text: Man lernt nie aus
english_translation: One never stops learning
Cultural_Context: Learning is a lifelong process — stay humble and open.

source_text: Der Schein trügt
english_translation: Appearances deceive
Cultural_Context: Things are not always as they seem — don't judge by surface.

source_text: Alle Wege führen nach Rom
english_translation: All roads lead to Rome
Cultural_Context: There are many ways to achieve the same goal.

source_text: Das Leben ist kein Ponyhof
english_translation: Life is not a pony farm
Cultural_Context: Life is hard and full of disappointments — no sugarcoating.

source_text: Erst denken, dann handeln
english_translation: First think, then act
Cultural_Context: Consider consequences before acting impulsively.

source_text: Wer rastet, der rostet
english_translation: He who rests, rusts
Cultural_Context: Inactivity leads to decline — stay active and engaged.

source_text: Das Auge isst mit
english_translation: The eye eats too
Cultural_Context: Food looks better when presented well — presentation matters.

source_text: Reden ist Silber, Schweigen ist Gold
english_translation: Speech is silver, silence is gold
Cultural_Context: Silence is often more valuable than speaking — knowing when to stay quiet shows wisdom.

source_text: Wer nicht hören will, muss fühlen
english_translation: He who doesn't want to hear must feel
Cultural_Context: If someone ignores advice or warnings, they will learn the hard way through consequences.

source_text: Der Krug geht so lange zum Brunnen, bis er bricht
english_translation: The jug goes to the well so often until it breaks
Cultural_Context: Bad habits or risky behavior eventually lead to failure or punishment.

source_text: Ein Unglück kommt selten allein
english_translation: Misfortune rarely comes alone
Cultural_Context: Bad things tend to happen in clusters — one problem often leads to more.

source_text: Der Mensch ist ein Gewohnheitstier
english_translation: Man is a creature of habit
Cultural_Context: People tend to stick to routines and patterns — change is difficult.

source_text: Krummes Holz gibt auch gerades Feuer
english_translation: Crooked wood also makes straight fire
Cultural_Context: Even imperfect or flawed materials can produce good results — make the best of what you have.

source_text: Des Teufels liebstes Möbelstück ist die lange Bank
english_translation: The devil’s favorite piece of furniture is the long bench
Cultural_Context: Procrastination is the devil’s tool — delaying tasks leads to trouble.

source_text: Selbst ist der Mann
english_translation: Self is the man
Cultural_Context: Do it yourself — self-reliance and independence are highly valued.

source_text: Ich kriege so eine Krawatte
english_translation: I get such a tie
Cultural_Context: I’m getting so annoyed or angry (colloquial expression for irritation).

source_text: Bis über beide Ohren verliebt sein
english_translation: To be over both ears in love
Cultural_Context: To be completely, head-over-heels in love.

source_text: Die beleidigte Leberwurst spielen
english_translation: To play the offended liver sausage
Cultural_Context: To sulk or overreact dramatically to something small.

source_text: Der Hunger kommt beim Essen
english_translation: Appetite comes while eating
Cultural_Context: Motivation and energy grow once you start working on something.

source_text: Sich die Wurst vom Brot nehmen lassen
english_translation: To let someone take the sausage off your bread
Cultural_Context: To let someone take advantage of you or walk all over you.

source_text: Das ist mir Wurst
english_translation: That is sausage to me
Cultural_Context: I don’t care / it doesn’t matter to me.

source_text: Um den heißen Brei herumreden
english_translation: To talk around the hot porridge
Cultural_Context: To beat around the bush instead of speaking directly.

source_text: Du gehst mir auf den Keks
english_translation: You’re getting on my cookie
Cultural_Context: You’re annoying me or getting on my nerves.

source_text: Das ist nicht mein Bier
english_translation: That’s not my beer
Cultural_Context: That’s not my problem / not my concern.

source_text: Dienst ist Dienst und Schnaps ist Schnaps
english_translation: Work is work and liquor is liquor
Cultural_Context: Separate professional duty from personal pleasure — keep boundaries.

source_text: Da steppt der Bär
english_translation: There the bear is stepping
Cultural_Context: It’s lively / the party is happening / things are really going on.

source_text: Wenn der Reiter nichts taugt, ist das Pferd schuld
english_translation: If the rider is no good, it’s the horse’s fault
Cultural_Context: Blaming tools or others for your own failure or incompetence.

source_text: Wer zwei Hasen auf einmal jagt bekommt keinen
english_translation: He who chases two hares at once catches none
Cultural_Context: Don’t divide your attention — focus on one task at a time.

source_text: Kümmere Dich nicht um ungelegte Eier
english_translation: Don’t worry about eggs that haven’t been laid yet
Cultural_Context: Don’t worry about future problems that haven’t happened yet.

source_text: Du siehst den Wald vor lauter Bäumen nicht
english_translation: You don’t see the forest for all the trees
Cultural_Context: You’re missing the big picture by focusing on small details.

source_text: Bäume wachsen nicht in den Himmel
english_translation: Trees don’t grow into the sky
Cultural_Context: There are natural limits to growth or ambition.

source_text: Gut Ding will Weile haben
english_translation: Good things take time
Cultural_Context: Quality work or results require patience and time.

source_text: Aus Schaden wird man klug
english_translation: From damage one becomes wise
Cultural_Context: Mistakes and failures are the best teachers.

source_text: Taten sagen mehr als Worte
english_translation: Actions speak louder than words
Cultural_Context: What you do is more important than what you say.

source_text: Das Billige ist immer das Teuerste
english_translation: The cheap is always the most expensive
Cultural_Context: Buying low-quality things ends up costing more in the long run.

source_text: Anfangen ist leicht, Beharren eine Kunst
english_translation: Starting is easy, persistence is an art
Cultural_Context: The real skill is finishing what you start.

source_text: Man muss die Dinge nehmen, wie sie kommen
english_translation: You have to take things as they come
Cultural_Context: Accept life’s events without resistance or over-worrying.

source_text: Alle wissen guten Rath, Nur nicht, wer ihn nöthig hat
english_translation: Everyone knows good advice, but not the one who needs it
Cultural_Context: Advice is easy to give to others but hard to follow when you need it yourself.

source_text: Allein ist besser als mit Schlechten im Verein
english_translation: Better alone than in bad company
Cultural_Context: Solitude is preferable to bad company, but good company is better than being alone.

source_text: Am vielen Lachen erkennt man den Narren
english_translation: A fool is ever laughing
Cultural_Context: Fools are recognized by their constant laughter and lack of seriousness.

source_text: An den Früchten erkennt man den Baum
english_translation: The apple does not fall far from the tree
Cultural_Context: Children resemble their parents in behavior and character.

source_text: Anfangen ist leicht, beharren eine Kunst
english_translation: To begin is easy, to persist is an art
Cultural_Context: Starting something is simple, but continuing and finishing requires skill and discipline.

source_text: Angebotene Waare stinkt
english_translation: Proffered service stinks
Cultural_Context: Unsolicited offers are often unwelcome or suspicious.

source_text: Arzt, hilf dir selber
english_translation: Physician, heal thyself
Cultural_Context: Do not criticize others for faults you have yourself.

source_text: Auch der kleinste Feind ist nicht zu verachten
english_translation: There is no little enemy
Cultural_Context: Even small enemies or problems should not be underestimated.

source_text: Auf einen groben Klotz gehört ein grober Keil
english_translation: You must meet roughness with roughness
Cultural_Context: Respond to rudeness or harshness with equal firmness.

source_text: Aus den Augen, aus dem Sinn
english_translation: Out of sight, out of mind
Cultural_Context: Things or people fade from memory when they are no longer visible.

source_text: Aufgewärmter Kohl war niemals gut
english_translation: Reheated cabbage was never good
Cultural_Context: Rehashing old issues or ideas rarely leads to good results.

source_text: Aufschub bringt Gefahr
english_translation: There is danger in delay
Cultural_Context: Postponing action can lead to missed opportunities or worse problems.

source_text: Aus einer Mücke einen Elefanten machen
english_translation: To make an elephant out of a fly
Cultural_Context: Exaggerating minor issues into major problems.

source_text: Bald geben, ist doppelt geben
english_translation: He gives twice who gives quickly
Cultural_Context: Quick generosity or help has double the value.

source_text: Bald reif hält nicht steif
english_translation: Early ripe, early rotten
Cultural_Context: Precocious success or talent is often short-lived.

source_text: Barmherzigkeit fängt en zu Hause an
english_translation: Charity begins at home
Cultural_Context: Help and kindness should start with your own family.

source_text: Bedenke das Ende
english_translation: Whatever you do, act wisely, and consider the end
Cultural_Context: Always think about the consequences before acting.

source_text: Bedenke, dass du sterben musst
english_translation: Remember that you must die
Cultural_Context: Contemplate mortality to live wisely.

source_text: Behüte mich Gott vor meinen Freunden, mit den Feinden will ich schon fertig werden
english_translation: Defend me from my friends, from my enemies I can defend myself
Cultural_Context: Friends can sometimes cause more harm than enemies.

source_text: Bei offener Kiste mag auch der Fromme ein Schalk werden
english_translation: A nice wife and a back door oft make a rich man poor
Cultural_Context: Temptations in the home can lead to ruin.

source_text: Berühre nicht alte Wunden
english_translation: It is not wise to open old wounds
Cultural_Context: Avoid reopening past hurts or arguments.

source_text: Besser arm in Ehren als reich in Schanden
english_translation: Better poor in honor than rich in shame
Cultural_Context: Integrity and honor are more important than wealth gained dishonestly.

source_text: Besser ein Narr mit allen andern, als ein Weiser und allein
english_translation: Better a fool with everyone else than a wise man and alone
Cultural_Context: It's better to fit in than to be isolated in wisdom.

source_text: Besser ein Spatz in der Hand, als eine Taube auf dem Dach
english_translation: A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush
Cultural_Context: Certainty is better than risky prospects.

source_text: Blinder Eifer ist Feuer ohne Licht
english_translation: Zeal without knowledge is a runaway horse
Cultural_Context: Blind enthusiasm without understanding is dangerous.

source_text: Blut ist dicker als Wasser
english_translation: Blood is thicker than water
Cultural_Context: Family bonds are stronger than other relationships.

source_text: Blödes Herz buhlt keine schöne Frau
english_translation: Faint heart never won fair lady
Cultural_Context: Courage is needed to win affection or success.

source_text: Böses mit Gutem vergelten
english_translation: Repay evil with good
Cultural_Context: Respond to negativity with kindness.

source_text: Da liegt der Hund begraben
english_translation: To smell a rat
Cultural_Context: Suspect hidden problems or motives.

source_text: Das Auge sieht weit, der Verstand noch weiter
english_translation: The eye looks but it is the mind that sees
Cultural_Context: Insight and understanding go beyond mere observation.

source_text: Das Bessere ist der Feind des guten
english_translation: Better is the enemy of good
Cultural_Context: Perfectionism can prevent completion of good work.

source_text: Das Beste kommt selten hernach
english_translation: The best is seldom the last
Cultural_Context: Good opportunities or results don't always come last.

source_text: Das böse Gewissen verrät sich selbst
english_translation: A guilty conscience needs no accuser
Cultural_Context: Guilt shows itself outwardly without needing accusation.

source_text: Das Eisen schmieden, solange es heiß ist
english_translation: Strike while the iron is hot
Cultural_Context: Act at the right moment when conditions are favorable.

source_text: Das Glück hilft den Kühnen
english_translation: Fortune favors the bold
Cultural_Context: Courage and boldness bring success.

source_text: Das Herz lügt nicht
english_translation: The heart does not lie
Cultural_Context: Instinct and inner feeling are truthful.

source_text: Das Kind mit dem Bade ausschütten
english_translation: Don't throw out the child with the bath water
Cultural_Context: Avoid excess in correction — don't discard the good with the bad.

source_text: Das Pferd stirbt oft, ehe das Gras wächst
english_translation: While the grass grows the steed starves
Cultural_Context: Delays in help or rewards cause loss.

source_text: Das Weib ist des Mannes größtes Glück oder Unglück
english_translation: Choose a wife rather by your ear than your eye
Cultural_Context: Character is more important than appearance in a partner.

source_text: Das Wort verhallt, die Schrift bleibt
english_translation: Paper is forbearing
Cultural_Context: Written words endure while spoken ones fade.

source_text: Die zeiten änder sich, und wir ändern uns in ihnen
english_translation: Times change and we are changed with them
Cultural_Context: Adaptation to change is necessary.

source_text: Deine Wäsche wasche zu Hause
english_translation: Don't wash your dirty linen in public
Cultural_Context: Handle private matters privately.

source_text: Dem Beichtwater, Arzt unt Advokaten darf man nichts verschweigen
english_translation: Hide nothing from thy minister, physician and lawyer
Cultural_Context: Be honest with advisors and professionals.

source_text: Dem Hahn, der zu früh kräht, dreht man den Hals um
english_translation: A cock that crows too early gets a twisted neck
Cultural_Context: Patience avoids premature action or punishment.

source_text: Der Amboss erschrickt vor dem Hammer nicht
english_translation: A good anvil does not fear the hammer
Cultural_Context: Strength and resilience withstand force.

source_text: Der Fisch stinkt vom Kopf her
english_translation: A fish stinks from the head
Cultural_Context: Problems originate from leadership or the top.

source_text: Der Geizige ist keinem gut, ihm selbst der Ärgste
english_translation: The covetous man is good to none and worst to himself
Cultural_Context: Greed harms the greedy most.

source_text: Der Gesunde weiß nicht, wie reich er ist
english_translation: Health is wealth
Cultural_Context: Good health is invaluable and often taken for granted.

source_text: Alein ist besser als mit Schlechten im Verein
english_translation: Better to be alone than in bad company
Cultural_Context: It is preferable to be by oneself or in the company of good people rather than with bad ones, emphasizing the value of positive associations.

source_text: Aller guten Dinge sind drei
english_translation: All good things come in threes
Cultural_Context: Good things or events often occur in sets of three, reflecting a cultural belief in triadic patterns and persistence.

source_text: Alles ist seinen Preis wert
english_translation: Everything is worth its price
Cultural_Context: Items or actions are valued according to what someone is willing to pay or the effort involved.

source_text: Alles zu seiner Zeit
english_translation: Everything in its season
Cultural_Context: Tasks and events should be addressed at the appropriate time, highlighting patience and timing.

source_text: Alte Füchse gehen schwer in die Falle
english_translation: An old fox understands a trap
Cultural_Context: Experienced individuals are wary and difficult to deceive or catch.

source_text: Alte soll man ehren, Junge soll man lehren
english_translation: Gray hairs are honorable; one should honor the old and teach the young
Cultural_Context: Respect for elders and education of youth are fundamental social duties.

source_text: Andere Länder, andere Sitten
english_translation: Other countries, other customs
Cultural_Context: When in a foreign place, adapt to local customs and behaviors.

source_text: Barmherzigkeit fängt zu Hause an
english_translation: Charity begins at home
Cultural_Context: Help should start with one's own family or household.

source_text: Die Zeiten ändern sich, und wir ändern uns in ihnen
english_translation: Times change and we are changed with them
Cultural_Context: Adaptation to changing times is essential for survival.

source_text: Klappe zu. Affe tot.
english_translation: Mouth shut. Monkey dead.
Cultural_Context: This is the end of the conversation (like 'and Bob’s your uncle!').

source_text: Schwein gehabt
english_translation: Pig had
Cultural_Context: To be lucky (have a stroke of luck).

source_text: Jemanden etwas aus der Nase ziehen
english_translation: To pull something out of someone’s nose
Cultural_Context: To tediously extract information from someone.

source_text: Blau sein
english_translation: To be blue
Cultural_Context: To be drunk.

source_text: Nicht mehr alle Tassen im Schrank haben
english_translation: To not have all the cups in the cupboard
Cultural_Context: To not be quite right in the head (crazy).

source_text: Da wird ja der Hund in der Pfanne verrückt!
english_translation: That will make the dog in the pan crazy!
Cultural_Context: When something is shocking or unbelievable (in a bad way).

source_text: Einen Vogel haben
english_translation: To have a bird
Cultural_Context: To be crazy.

source_text: Friede, Freude, Eierkuchen
english_translation: Peace, joy, pancake
Cultural_Context: Love, peace and harmony (everything is perfect).

source_text: Eine Extrawurst haben
english_translation: To have an extra sausage
Cultural_Context: To get special treatment.

source_text: Seinen Senf dazugeben
english_translation: To give his mustard
Cultural_Context: To give one’s opinion (unasked).

source_text: Eine beleidigte Leberwurst zu spielen
english_translation: To play the offended liver sausage
Cultural_Context: To react in an exaggerated or insulted manner during an argument.

source_text: Ich verstehe nur Bahnhof
english_translation: I only understand train station
Cultural_Context: I don’t understand (something complex or noisy).

source_text: Butter bei die Fische
english_translation: Butter at the fishes
Cultural_Context: Get to the point (make something complete and clear).

source_text: Die besten Schwimmer ertrinken
english_translation: The best swimmers drown
Cultural_Context: Even experts can fail (work smarter, not harder).

source_text: Aus einem Stein ist schwer Öl pressen
english_translation: It’s hard to press oil out of a stone
Cultural_Context: Impossible tasks (you can’t get blood from a stone).

source_text: Die Arznei ist oft ärger als das Übel
english_translation: The drug is often worse than the disease
Cultural_Context: The cure can be worse than the disease.

source_text: Der Ertrinkende greift nach einem Strohhalm
english_translation: The drowning man reaches for the drinking straw
Cultural_Context: Desperate people clutch at straws.

source_text: Gesunder Mann, reicher Mann
english_translation: A healthy man is a rich man
Cultural_Context: Health is the greatest wealth.

source_text: Den Teufel nicht an die Wand malen
english_translation: Do not paint the devil on the wall
Cultural_Context: Do not assume something will go wrong before knowing the outcome.

source_text: Alles hat ein Ende, nur die Wurst hat zwei
english_translation: Everything has an end, only the sausage has two
Cultural_Context: All things must come to an end.

source_text: Morgenstund hat Gold im Mund
english_translation: The morning hour has gold in its mouth
Cultural_Context: Waking up early allows people to be more productive and successful.

source_text: Du siehst den Wald lauter Bäumen nicht
english_translation: You do not see the forest for the trees
Cultural_Context: People must look at the bigger picture instead of focusing on just one small aspect.

source_text: Kümmere dich nicht um ungelegte Eier
english_translation: Don't count your chickens before they hatch
Cultural_Context: Remain realistic about expectations rather than hoping for something that might never come to fruition.

source_text: Lebe wie du kannst, nicht wie du willst
english_translation: Live as you can, not as you want
Cultural_Context: You have to live in accordance to your opportunities and abilities.
